# A slice may be stored and read at an offset in the same forward loop when the
# offset is a positive constant: iteration i reads the element iteration i+d writes
# later, so it reads the value from before the loop, and the vector loop loads that
# before any store of the chunk, even when the body stores the slice first.
# A shift of a slice onto itself is the copy builtin. A loop over part of the
# slices checks only the part it touches for overlap, so views that overlap only
# outside it still take the vector loop, and views that overlap inside it take the
# original loop.

# The scalar program is the reference behavior.
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
cmpenv stderr stderr.want
cmp ops_simd.go ops_simd.go.want
cmp ops.go ops.go.guarded

# The simd build must behave identically.
env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

// Reads the element ahead of the one it writes, from the slice it writes.
func ShiftAdd(a, b []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		a[i] = a[i+1] + b[i]
	}
}

// Moves the elements after k down by one: a copy.
func ShiftLeft(a []int32, k int) {
	for i := k; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		a[i] = a[i+1]
	}
}

// The read of a[i+1] follows stores to a, but still sees the old value.
func ReadAfterStore(a, b, d []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		a[i] = b[i] + d[i]
		b[i] = a[i] * 2
		a[i] = b[i] + a[i+1]*d[i]
	}
}

// Both offset reads come before the store to a.
func Pair(a, x, y []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(a)-2; i++ {
		x[i] = a[i+2]
		a[i] = y[i] + a[i+1]
	}
}

// Only the first half of the slices is touched.
func AddHalf(b, xx, a []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(b)/2; i++ {
		b[i] = xx[i] + a[i]
	}
}
-- ops_simd.go.want --
//go:build goexperiment.simd

package test

import (
	"simd"
	"unsafe"
)

// Reads the element ahead of the one it writes, from the slice it writes.
func ShiftAdd(a, b []int32) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(a, b, 0, len(a)-1+1, 0, len(a)-1) {
		for i := 0; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
			a[i] = a[i+1] + b[i]
		}
	} else {
		if len(a)-1 > 0 {
			_ = a[(len(a)-1)-1]
			_ = a[len(a)-1]
			_ = b[(len(a)-1)-1]
			for _i := 0; _i < len(a)-1; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i+1:])
				_v2, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(b[_i : len(a)-1])
				_v1.Add(_v2).StorePart(a[_i : len(a)-1])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// Moves the elements after k down by one: a copy.
func ShiftLeft(a []int32, k int) {
	if len(a)-1 > k {
		_ = a[(len(a)-1)-1]
		_ = a[len(a)-1]
		copy(a[k:len(a)-1], a[k+1:])
	}
}

// The read of a[i+1] follows stores to a, but still sees the old value.
func ReadAfterStore(a, b, d []int32) {
	_vcInt32s2_1 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(2)
	if _loopvecOverlap(a, b, 0, len(a)-1+1, 0, len(a)-1) || _loopvecOverlap(a, d, 0, len(a)-1+1, 0, len(a)-1) || _loopvecOverlap(b, d, 0, len(a)-1, 0, len(a)-1) {
		for i := 0; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
			a[i] = b[i] + d[i]
			b[i] = a[i] * 2
			a[i] = b[i] + a[i+1]*d[i]
		}
	} else {
		if len(a)-1 > 0 {
			_ = a[(len(a)-1)-1]
			_ = b[(len(a)-1)-1]
			_ = d[(len(a)-1)-1]
			_ = a[len(a)-1]
			for _i := 0; _i < len(a)-1; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i+1:])
				_v2, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(b[_i : len(a)-1])
				_v3, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(d[_i : len(a)-1])
				_v2.Add(_v3).StorePart(a[_i : len(a)-1])
				_v4, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i : len(a)-1])
				_v4.Mul(_vcInt32s2_1).StorePart(b[_i : len(a)-1])
				_v5, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(b[_i : len(a)-1])
				_v1.Mul(_v3).Add(_v5).StorePart(a[_i : len(a)-1])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// Both offset reads come before the store to a.
func Pair(a, x, y []int32) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(x, a, 0, len(a)-2, 0, len(a)-2+2) || _loopvecOverlap(x, y, 0, len(a)-2, 0, len(a)-2) || _loopvecOverlap(a, y, 0, len(a)-2+2, 0, len(a)-2) {
		for i := 0; i < len(a)-2; i++ {
			x[i] = a[i+2]
			a[i] = y[i] + a[i+1]
		}
	} else {
		if len(a)-2 > 0 {
			_ = x[(len(a)-2)-1]
			_ = a[(len(a)-2)+1]
			_ = a[(len(a)-2)-1]
			_ = y[(len(a)-2)-1]
			_ = a[len(a)-2]
			for _i := 0; _i < len(a)-2; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i+2:])
				_v2, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i+1:])
				_v1.StorePart(x[_i : len(a)-2])
				_v3, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(y[_i : len(a)-2])
				_v3.Add(_v2).StorePart(a[_i : len(a)-2])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// Only the first half of the slices is touched.
func AddHalf(b, xx, a []int32) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(b, xx, 0, len(b)/2, 0, len(b)/2) || _loopvecOverlap(b, a, 0, len(b)/2, 0, len(b)/2) {
		for i := 0; i < len(b)/2; i++ {
			b[i] = xx[i] + a[i]
		}
	} else {
		if len(b)/2 > 0 {
			_ = b[(len(b)/2)-1]
			_ = xx[(len(b)/2)-1]
			_ = a[(len(b)/2)-1]
			for _i := 0; _i < len(b)/2; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(xx[_i : len(b)/2])
				_v2, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i : len(b)/2])
				_v1.Add(_v2).StorePart(b[_i : len(b)/2])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

func _loopvecOverlap[T any](a, b []T, window ...int) bool {
	aLo, aHi, bLo, bHi := 0, len(a), 0, len(b)
	if len(window) == 4 {
		aLo, aHi, bLo, bHi = window[0], window[1], window[2], window[3]
	}
	if aLo >= aHi || bLo >= bHi {
		return false
	}
	size := unsafe.Sizeof(a[0])
	aBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(a)))
	bBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(b)))
	aStart, aEnd := aBase+uintptr(aLo)*size, aBase+uintptr(aHi)*size
	bStart, bEnd := bBase+uintptr(bLo)*size, bBase+uintptr(bHi)*size
	return aStart < bEnd && bStart < aEnd
}
-- ops.go.guarded --
//go:build !goexperiment.simd

package test

// Reads the element ahead of the one it writes, from the slice it writes.
func ShiftAdd(a, b []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		a[i] = a[i+1] + b[i]
	}
}

// Moves the elements after k down by one: a copy.
func ShiftLeft(a []int32, k int) {
	for i := k; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		a[i] = a[i+1]
	}
}

// The read of a[i+1] follows stores to a, but still sees the old value.
func ReadAfterStore(a, b, d []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		a[i] = b[i] + d[i]
		b[i] = a[i] * 2
		a[i] = b[i] + a[i+1]*d[i]
	}
}

// Both offset reads come before the store to a.
func Pair(a, x, y []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(a)-2; i++ {
		x[i] = a[i+2]
		a[i] = y[i] + a[i+1]
	}
}

// Only the first half of the slices is touched.
func AddHalf(b, xx, a []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(b)/2; i++ {
		b[i] = xx[i] + a[i]
	}
}
-- stderr.want --
loopvec: rewrote 5 loop(s) in $WORK/ops.go
-- testmain/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/test"
)

var sizes = []int{0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 16, 17, 33, 64, 65, 100, 131}

func ramp(n int, scale int32) []int32 {
	s := make([]int32, n)
	for i := range s {
		s[i] = int32(i*i+1) * scale
	}
	return s
}

func sum(s []int32) (t int64) {
	for i, v := range s {
		t += int64(v) * int64(i+1)
	}
	return t
}

func try(f func()) (panicked bool) {
	defer func() { panicked = recover() != nil }()
	f()
	return false
}

// out is what a loop left in a slice, or 0 when it panicked: the rewritten loops
// check the lengths first and write nothing, where the scalar loop has written what
// came before the bad index. Only the panic is the same.
func out(panicked bool, s []int32) int64 {
	if panicked {
		return 0
	}
	return sum(s)
}

func main() {
	for _, n := range sizes {
		a, b := ramp(n, 3), ramp(n, 5)
		p := try(func() { test.ShiftAdd(a, b) })
		fmt.Println(n, "ShiftAdd", p, out(p, a))

		for _, k := range []int{0, 1, 3, n / 2, n} {
			a = ramp(n, 3)
			p = try(func() { test.ShiftLeft(a, k) })
			fmt.Println(n, "ShiftLeft", k, p, out(p, a))
		}

		a, x, y := ramp(n, 3), ramp(n, 7), ramp(n, 11)
		p = try(func() { test.Pair(a, x, y) })
		fmt.Println(n, "Pair", p, out(p, a), out(p, x))

		a, b, d := ramp(n, 3), ramp(n, 5), ramp(n, 7)
		p = try(func() { test.ReadAfterStore(a, b, d) })
		fmt.Println(n, "ReadAfterStore", p, out(p, a), out(p, b))

		// Short operands must panic.
		a, b = ramp(n, 3), ramp(n, 5)
		p = try(func() { test.ShiftAdd(a, b[:max(n-2, 0)]) })
		fmt.Println(n, "Short", p, out(p, a))

		// Views of one slice: the halves do not overlap in what the loop touches,
		// one view behind and one ahead overlap inside it.
		for _, view := range []int{0, 1, 2, 3} {
			buf := ramp(n+4, 1)
			c := ramp(n, 9)
			half := n / 2
			var p bool
			switch view {
			case 0:
				p = try(func() { test.AddHalf(buf[:n], buf[half:n], c) })
			case 1:
				p = try(func() { test.AddHalf(buf[1:n+1], buf[:n], c) })
			case 2:
				p = try(func() { test.AddHalf(buf[:n], buf[1:n+1], c) })
			case 3:
				p = try(func() { test.AddHalf(buf[:n], buf[:n], c) })
			}
			fmt.Println(n, "View", view, p, out(p, buf))
		}
	}
}
